items.name: Lighting console
items.what: A full-size desk with rows of faders, buttons, encoder wheels and a touchscreen, built to store every light cue of a show and play them back on command. The rental house's own listing calls it simply "MA lighting console", runs Linux, and is priced and shelved as a full-size control desk. It sits at the mixing position and is wired or networked out to the fixtures.
items.inShow: The desk the lighting operator runs the whole show from: every cue, fade and blackout is called from here, live or against a pre-set timeline.

items.name: DMX splitter (outdoor)
items.what: A DMX512 line splitter and signal booster in a weatherproof, IP-rated housing. A single DMX line can only drive a limited number of devices before the signal needs repeating; this box takes one incoming DMX universe and re-transmits it as several fresh, electrically isolated outputs, so a rig can branch out to many fixtures — outdoors, in the weather — without the far end of the line dropping out.
items.inShow: Placed where one console/node output has to feed several outdoor truss runs, or a fixture count near or above the standard's unit-load limit on a single line — splits and re-powers the signal so every branch reads clean, in a housing sealed against weather.

needs.text: mains or DC power to the splitter itself
one DMX universe in from the console or node
outdoor-rated connectors and cable glands kept properly seated and sealed in use — an IP rating is only as good as the connections made on site

items.name: DMX decoder
items.what: A DMX decoder reads DMX512 data addressed to it and converts it into a different kind of output — typically a constant-voltage or constant-current signal for RGB/RGBW LED strip, or a switched relay output — for devices that cannot read DMX directly. The rental house's own listing names it only "Decoder" with the code 2303; no independent UPlight product page for this model was found, so its exact output type, channel count and load rating are not confirmed. Owed: ask the rental house what it is meant to drive.
items.inShow: Sits at the load end of a DMX line wherever a non-DMX-native fixture — most often LED strip, or a relay-controlled practical — needs to answer to the console.

items.name: 12-channel dimmer / power distro
items.what: A cabinet of 12 mains power outputs, each independently switchable and/or dimmable by DMX — the traditional way to make non-LED lanterns fade, and also a safe, fused way to break mains power out to many circuits even where nothing is actually being dimmed. items.name: Art-Net / sACN node
items.product: Art-Net / sACN node (Ethernet to DMX) — not on the rental house's list; planned from another supplier for this show
items.what: A small box that sits between the network — a cable from the console or a laptop — and the DMX cables running out to the lamps. It receives Art-Net or sACN data, which is DMX carried over ordinary Ethernet, and turns it back into standard 5-pin DMX512 signal on several physical output ports, each one a separate 'universe' of up to 512 channels. In plain terms: it is the translator between the network cable from the control position and the DMX cable that actually reaches the lights.
items.inShow: For this production a node is planned from a supplier other than the rental house, sized for four DMX universes: one network cable in from the desk or laptop, four DMX runs out to the rig, instead of running four separate long DMX cables all the way from the console.

items.name: Truss tower
items.product: Truss tower on a base plate, default 6 m — our own rig stock, not on the rental house's price list
items.what: A vertical stack of the same box truss, standing on a weighted or bolted base plate, used to lift a horizontal truss run — or a single fixture — up off the ground without hanging it from the building. Towers carry a maximum height and a maximum load at that height together: taller means less load, and every tower needs its base plate, ballast or outrigger set sized to the specific height and load, per the maker's own tables.
items.inShow: Stands a truss run at the wings or over the stage where there is no rigging point above — carries lighting, and sometimes speakers, on a freestanding leg.
